lines.text: Paul resolves to go to Jerusalem through Macedonia and Achaia, then to see Rome, and sends Timothy and Erastus ahead.
Demetrius, a silversmith who made shrines of Artemis, tells the craftsmen that Paul has persuaded many people in Asia to turn away.
The enraged men shout, and the crowd rushes into the theatre dragging Gaius and Aristarchus, but the disciples will not let Paul go before the assembly.
The Jews push Alexander forward, but the crowd shouts "Great is Artemis" for about three hours once they realize he is a Jew.
The city clerk calms the crowd, tells Demetrius to take complaints to the synagogue, warns of a charge of rioting, and dismisses the assembly.
